take: Brent holding a touch above $104 with the Strait of Hormuz still constrained is the dominant story, and the White House weighing the Defense Production Act with US refineries at 98% utilisation and diesel above $6/gal tells you the product market is the real squeeze point, not crude. The shipping angle is the Houthi mobilisation at Bab el-Mandeb alongside a 208% jump in Black Sea drifting drone discoveries in six months, which together push tonne-miles and war-risk premia higher and feed straight back into delivered bunker and freight costs. On positioning, the EIA's 13.8m b/d US crude record for 2026 and Nigeria's seven-fold rise in seaborne product exports since 2023 both point to non-OPEC and Atlantic Basin barrels filling the Gulf gap, so watch whether paper length in Brent is matched by physical replacement or is simply riding the risk premium. The cross-market link to watch is gasoil versus bunker: with diesel above $6/gal and refiners maxed out, any further escalation pulls VLSFO and MGO higher in tandem, whilst the Asyad MR newbuild programme to eight charter-backed ships signals owners are already pricing sustained product tonne-mile demand. In the next 24 hours, watch for any concrete US-Saudi action at Bab el-Mandeb, further Hormuz transit data, and whether the Defense Production Act talk firms into an actual announcement, any of which could move the flat price and the prompt gasoil crack sharply.
